events.factual_description: National Sawdust presents Eleanor Alberga: The String Quartet Cycle with support from Solaris on Friday, October 30, 2026. Doors are at 18:30 and the seated performance begins at 19:30 at 80 North 6th St, Brooklyn. The Green Room Ensemble program centers on Alberga's String Quartets Nos. 1, 2 and 3 and Piano Quintet No. 2 'Stark,' with Alberga at the piano alongside Thomas Bowes and Nathan Meltzer on violins, Jordan Bak on viola, and Sterling Elliott on cello. National Sawdust describes the project using U.S.-premiere-cycle and world-premiere language. Primary tour and performer sources, however, document the same ensemble and program at multiple North American dates from October 23 through November 1, including an October 23 Brannan Center performance that uses the same premiere framing. This record therefore preserves the program and project context without asserting that the October 30 Brooklyn performance itself is the chronological world or U.S. premiere. National Sawdust's page also contains a stale 'This event has passed' line while labeling the event UPCOMING and listing it on the current future performances calendar.

en.why_it_matters: The hook is hearing Alberga's chamber language as a body of work rather than a single piece: all three string quartets in one program, then the sound widened into a piano quintet with the composer herself at the keyboard. That makes the night a concentrated encounter with a living composer's instrumental voice, not a generic chamber recital.
en.trip_verdict: If New York is already viable on October 30, actively make room for National Sawdust and build the Brooklyn evening around the cycle. From the DMV, pair it with another strong New York reason rather than make a dedicated trip for this date alone, especially because the same project is touring several North American cities.

es.why_it_matters: La clave es escuchar el lenguaje de cámara de Alberga como un cuerpo de obra y no como una pieza aislada: los tres cuartetos de cuerda en un mismo programa y, después, la expansión hacia el quinteto con piano con la propia compositora al teclado. Eso convierte la noche en un encuentro concentrado con la identidad instrumental de una compositora viva, no en un recital de cámara genérico.
es.trip_verdict: Si Nueva York ya es viable el 30 de octubre, sí le haría espacio activamente a National Sawdust y armaría la noche en Brooklyn alrededor del ciclo. Desde el DMV lo combinaría con otra razón fuerte para subir, en vez de hacer un viaje dedicado únicamente por esta fecha, sobre todo porque el mismo proyecto recorre varias ciudades de Norteamérica.

priority_review.rationale: The specific live value is the complete three-quartet cycle plus Piano Quintet No. 2 with Alberga herself at the piano. A second editorial challenge tested the premiere language against primary tour evidence. A+ remains sufficient: the same ensemble and program are documented on a North American run from October 23 through November 1, with dates before and after Brooklyn, so October 30 is not established as an unlikely-to-recur or terminal opportunity. Actively making room is warranted; protect-the-night scarcity is not.
